candidates.title: The test-support surface has two activation regimes: cobre-core, cobre-io and cobre-stochastic pin the feature with a self dev-dependency while cobre-sddp and cobre-solver leave it to the command line

evidence.command: git grep -n 'path = "\."' 077dbe2c -- 'crates/*/Cargo.toml' | sed 's#^[a-f0-9]*:##'; git grep -n 'cfg(feature = "test-support")' 077dbe2c -- crates/cobre-solver/src | sed 's#^[a-f0-9]*:##'; git grep -l 'cobre_sddp::test_support' 077dbe2c -- 'crates/cobre-sddp/tests/*.rs' | wc -l; git grep -n 'cobre_solver::test_support' 077dbe2c -- 'crates/cobre-solver/tests/*.rs' | sed 's#^[a-f0-9]*:##'; git grep -n 'cobre-solver/test-support' 077dbe2c -- Cargo.toml 'crates/*/Cargo.toml'
evidence.reading: Five crates declare the feature (declarerAnchors: cobre-core Cargo.toml:30, cobre-io :33, cobre-sddp :55, cobre-solver :31, cobre-stochastic :26) but only three make it self-activating: cobre-core:40, cobre-io:54 and cobre-stochastic:42 each carry `<crate> = { path = ".", features = ["test-support"] }` in their own [dev-dependencies], so the gated surface is present in every dev build of those crates. cobre-sddp's [dev-dependencies] (Cargo.toml:74-90) enables test-support only on cobre-core (:77), never on itself, and cobre-solver's (Cargo.toml:51-52) holds matrixmultiply alone. The `test` arm of `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]` covers only in-crate unit tests: an integration binary links the lib as an ordinary dependency, for which `test` is unset, so the 24 depth-1 cobre-sddp binaries that import cobre_sddp::test_support and the 2 cobre-solver binaries that import cobre_solver::test_support (tests/conformance.rs:32, tests/_clp_sign_convention_probe.rs:21) resolve that import only when --features test-support arrives on the command line; the workspace command in CLAUDE.md and NON_SOLVER_FEATURES in .github/workflows/ci.yml:32 both supply it, so CI is green and the asymmetry is invisible there. No cargo command was run for this candidate: the consequence follows from the manifests, the cfg predicates and Cargo's feature resolution. cobre-solver is the sharpest instance: it is the only crate whose src/ gates the surface with the narrower `#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]` (src/lib.rs:163, src/backends/highs/solver.rs:6 and :580 — every other declarer's src/ uses the wide predicate) and no manifest anywhere enables cobre-solver/test-support (inventory perCrate.cobre-solver.consumesTestSupport = false). Two crate-local promises are narrower than they read: cobre-sddp/Cargo.toml:51-53 and crates/cobre-sddp/src/test_support.rs:9-10 both say the builders are reachable by plain `cargo test` and by downstream integration tests via the feature, which holds for the crate's unit tests and for downstream crates carrying the dev-dep, but not for the crate's own 24 consuming integration binaries. This is the tree state behind the §2.3 Absent bullet (docs/design/testing-architecture.md:99-100, 'the test-support feature exists but is applied inconsistently'): the claim holds, and the inconsistency is the activation path, not the declaration. Adjacent, not re-raised: the mirror item 'Python-binding Rust tests invisible to CI' residue (b) records the same missing-dev-dep shape for crates/cobre-python/Cargo.toml:34.

candidates.fixShape: Unify the feature surface. Give cobre-sddp and cobre-solver the same self dev-dependency the other three declarers carry, so each crate's own integration binaries see the gated surface in every dev build instead of depending on a command-line flag, and widen cobre-solver's three src/ gates to the predicate every other declarer uses unless the raw FFI handle is deliberately narrowed. Then correct the two crate-local promises to say which builds reach the builders. No test is added, removed, renamed, skipped or weakened and no baseline moves, so cargo nextest list --features test-support reports the same count before and after.

candidates.title: The yardstick's §2.2 map says every crate other than cobre-sddp constructs fixtures per-file, but cobre-stochastic and cobre-io each carry a shared multi-binary harness module at the pin

evidence.command: git show 077dbe2c:docs/design/testing-architecture.md | sed -n '72,78p'; git grep -n '^mod helpers;\|^mod common;' 077dbe2c -- 'crates/*/tests/*.rs' | sed 's#^[a-f0-9]*:##' | awk -F/ '{print $2}' | sort | uniq -c; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-stochastic/tests/common/mod.rs | wc -l; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-io/tests/helpers/mod.rs | wc -l
evidence.output:
`cobre-sddp` is the sole home of: all four test tiers, the only large
`tests/common/` harness (`StubComm`/`Rank0Of2`, `build_setup_*`, `make_*`
builders, `parity_hash`, `permute`), the only `tests/fixtures/` (dual golden

(with its power self-checks), and the only `benches/`. Every other crate is unit

- behavioral only, constructing fixtures per-file.

evidence.reading: The §2.2 sentence at docs/design/testing-architecture.md:76-78 is present tense and unqualified: 'Every other crate is unit- / behavioral only, constructing fixtures per-file.' At the pin two other crates share a harness module instead. crates/cobre-stochastic/tests/common/mod.rs is 261 lines and is declared by 8 of the crate's 9 depth-1 binaries (conformance.rs:9, forward_sampler.rs:15, forward_sampler_golden.rs:17, halton_integration.rs:26, lhs_integration.rs:26, reproducibility.rs:16, saa_golden_value.rs:15, sobol_integration.rs:26; par_a_historical_replay.rs is the exception). crates/cobre-io/tests/helpers/mod.rs is 204 lines and is declared by 6 of that crate's 12 binaries (integration.rs:10, invariance.rs:14, load_case_productivity_resolution.rs:9, load_case_scalar_parameters.rs:5, post_study_stages.rs:17, resolver_builder_index_alignment.rs:18). The measurement handle is the inventory's own binary-versus-file disagreement: cobre-stochastic is 9 binaries but 10 files and cobre-io is 12 binaries but 13 files, and in each crate the extra file is exactly this harness module (git ls-tree -r over the two tests/ trees returns crates/cobre-io/tests/helpers/mod.rs and crates/cobre-stochastic/tests/common/mod.rs as the only non-depth-1 .rs files besides cobre-sddp's five). The drift matters because the §5.2 target plan is written from this map and names only one migration source, 'cobre-sddp/tests/common/ collapses into cobre-sddp's test-support surface' (docs/design/testing-architecture.md:417-421): a collapse driven by that list leaves the other two harnesses unaccounted for. §2.2 is a current-state claim class (claim-classes.json row ta-2.2-other-crates-per-file-fixtures, class current-state, driftIsFinding true), so contradiction by the tree is prose-drift. Related adjudicate row recorded, not decided: ta-5.2-adoption-uniform (docs/design/testing-architecture.md:425-431), the Adoption paragraph that already records two uncarried bullets.

candidates.fixShape: Re-home the map, not the tests: restate §2.2 so it names all three shared harness modules and says what distinguishes cobre-sddp's (it owns its fixtures) from the other two (they re-export a crate's test_support surface), then extend the §5.2 collapse source list to match. Prose and plan-text only; no test file moves under this candidate, so the test count and every assertion are untouched.

candidates.title: One shared-harness role carries two directory names and three compositions, and the differently-named cobre-io harness is invisible to a migration that greps for tests/common

evidence.command: git ls-tree --name-only -r 077dbe2c crates/cobre-io/tests crates/cobre-stochastic/tests crates/cobre-sddp/tests | grep -E '/(common|helpers)/'; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-io/tests/helpers/mod.rs | sed -n '1,13p'; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-stochastic/tests/common/mod.rs | sed -n '6,20p'
evidence.reading: The three crates with a shared integration harness solve the same problem three ways. Naming: cobre-sddp and cobre-stochastic use tests/common/, cobre-io uses tests/helpers/ — the same role under two directory names, so the §5.2 collapse target 'cobre-sddp/tests/common/' (docs/design/testing-architecture.md:417-421) and any grep written from it sees neither of the other two. Composition: cobre-sddp's harness owns its fixtures across five files (mod.rs 320 lines declaring the submodules at :25-28, builders.rs 383, parity_hash.rs 417, permute.rs 204, anticipated_structural_assertions.rs 181 — 1,505 lines, including the StubComm Communicator impl at mod.rs:32), while cobre-io's (204 lines) and cobre-stochastic's (261 lines) are mostly re-export shims over a src/ test_support module plus two or three local case builders — cobre-io has therefore already done most of the §5.2 collapse while keeping a directory the plan does not name. All three need a crate-level #![allow(dead_code)] (cobre-sddp tests/common/mod.rs:6, cobre-stochastic tests/common/mod.rs:6, cobre-io tests/helpers/mod.rs:2) because a tests/ harness module is source-included per binary rather than linked once, which is the mechanism the two rationale comments state correctly. The measurement handle is cobre-io's binary-versus-file delta (12 depth-1 binaries, 13 recursive files); the extra file is tests/helpers/mod.rs. This is the tree state behind the §3.2 findings the yardstick already records (claim-classes.json rows ta-3.2.2-no-crate-standard at docs/design/testing-architecture.md:135-139 and ta-3.2.3-fixture-fragmentation at :140-145), a current-state class the tree agrees with, so the fact itself is the smell. Not raised here and cross-referenced instead: the mirror item 'Oracle test-harness duplication' covers the four fn close carriers inside cobre-sddp/tests, and TD-030 / TD-043 cover byte-identical per-file preludes; this candidate is about the harness directory's identity, not about duplicated bodies.

candidates.fixShape: Pick one directory name for the role and re-home the odd one, so a single convention statement and a single grep reach every shared harness; record in the §5.2 plan which of the three compositions each crate is expected to end at, since two are already re-export shims and one owns its fixtures. Re-homing a harness module renames no test and changes no assertion, so the nextest count and every retained claim are unchanged.
